title: Henry Hatsworth in the Puzzling Adventure
subtitle: An adventurer has trouble on both screens
summary: Henry Hatsworth in the Puzzling Adventure is EA Tiburon's Nintendo DS combination of action platforming and a block-matching puzzle game. Its gentleman explorer searches for pieces of a golden suit linked to the Puzzle Realm, with the upper screen following his physical adventure and the lower one receiving its consequences. Defeated enemies become blocks that must be dealt with below. The two games therefore share a practical problem: success in a fight does not finish the work if its remains are allowed to build into another threat on the touchscreen.
body: Henry Hatsworth in the Puzzling Adventure is EA Tiburon's Nintendo DS combination of action platforming and a block-matching puzzle game. Its gentleman explorer searches for pieces of a golden suit linked to the Puzzle Realm, with the upper screen following his physical adventure and the lower one receiving its consequences. Defeated enemies become blocks that must be dealt with below. The two games therefore share a practical problem: success in a fight does not finish the work if its remains are allowed to build into another threat on the touchscreen.

The lower grid rises as play continues, and enemy blocks reaching its upper edge can revive in Hatsworth's world. Swapping blocks into matching groups removes them and contributes energy to the Super Meter. The player has to judge when the platforming situation permits attention to move below, then clear enough space to keep the earlier victories secure. Special blocks can help or hinder the adventurer, making the puzzle board another source of immediate consequences. The connection gives matching colours a purpose beyond improving a separate score at the bottom of the display.

Filling the Super Meter restores a younger, stronger Hatsworth, while charging it further allows Tea Time to summon a powerful robot suit. The comic transformation converts successful puzzle work into a brief advantage in the action game. Money found during the adventure can also purchase upgrades at his assistant's shop. These systems give the two halves a shared economy: enemies, energy and rewards move between them, so a well-managed puzzle can prepare the next stretch of platforming rather than merely interrupting it with an unrelated activity.
